sourcePin.title: ARM architecture family

sourcePin.limitation: Documented architecture and explanations, not proprietary implementation access or a physical teardown

reasons: Draft claims 'ARM AArch32 is a 32-bit RISC instruction set architecture introduced in 1985' but source shows ARM family introduced 1985; AArch32 as a named 32-bit execution state was formalized with ARMv8 (2011) per infobox.

Draft states 'register file of 15 general-purpose 32-bit registers plus a link register, with the program counter separate' but source infobox says '15 × 32-bit integer registers, including R14 (link register), but not R15 (PC)' meaning PC is R15, not separate.

Draft claims 'Thumb-2 mode which mixes 16-bit and 32-bit instructions' and 'processor switching between modes using branch-and-link instructions or state-bit manipulation in the program counter' but source only notes encoding uses mixed 16/32-bit instructions, no mechanism for switching described.

Draft lists 'Jazelle for Java bytecode handling, various DSP and cryptography extensions, and floating-point units' as extensions but source marks Jazelle and Thumb as 'obsolete since ARMv8' in AArch32 infobox.

Draft states 'AArch32 operates in a bi-endian mode with little-endian as default' and 'serves as the 32-bit complement to the 64-bit AArch64' but source shows bi-endian for both AArch32 and AArch64 infoboxes, not a distinguishing feature.
